Documentation → FortiWeb: Policies & Protection → Clone & migrate

Cloning & migrating server policies

Copy a server policy and its whole object tree on the same FortiWeb, onto another FortiWeb, or migrate it there — with a pre-flight checklist, a mandatory dry run, dummy VIP addresses and a reconciliation report.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsnetwork.edit network.apply protection.edit protection.apply users.manage
📍 WhereFortiWeb ADOM → FortiWeb → Policy → Server Policy → Clone, Clone to or Migrate to on the toolbar (URL /workspace/<appliance_id>; deep link /workspace/<appliance_id>?act=<action>&policy=<name>)

What is it?#

Three buttons on the toolbar of the Server Policy list copy a policy together with everything it references: Clone, Clone to and Migrate to. Their dialogs are titled Clone (same box), Clone to another FortiWeb and Migrate to another FortiWeb. A guided dialog runs a pre-flight checklist, asks only what it needs (name, VIP address, interface mapping, profile handling), requires a dry-run preview, and then runs the copy as a background job with a per-object reconciliation report.

What does it do?#

  • Walks the policy's whole tree on the source — virtual server and VIPs, server pool and members, health checks, content routing and, optionally, the Web Protection Profile with its sub-profiles — and creates on the destination what is missing there.
  • Leaves the copied policy disabled, so it cannot take traffic before a manual cutover.
  • Rewrites the VIP address of the copy to a dummy address following the administrator's rules (always in a bulk run; as a prefilled suggestion for a single policy).
  • Migrate clones first and, only if the copy landed cleanly, disables the source policy. The source is never deleted.
  • Never overwrites an object the destination already has. With Only add what is missing (on by default) it does not even add rows to it.
  • Records every run in the policy's Clone history badge and in a reconciliation report: planned vs created vs verified on the device.
Button (dialog) Writes to Name of the copy Source afterwards
Clone (Clone (same box)) Same FortiWeb You choose (default <name>-copy); bulk: <name>-copy Unchanged
Clone to (Clone to another FortiWeb) Destination Same name unless you change it (single only) Unchanged
Migrate to (Migrate to another FortiWeb) Destination Same name unless you change it (single only) Disabled if the clone was clean

Requirements#

  • A FortiWeb selected as the current device; the Server Policy list is FortiWeb → Policy → Server Policy in the sidebar (the group's only entry, FortiWeb → Server Policy, while no GUI layout is imported for the device's build).
  • For Clone to and Migrate to: at least one other FortiWeb visible to you. Otherwise these buttons are disabled (No other FortiWeb is registered).
  • The source must answer live. A clone is never built from cached data; an unreachable source blocks the checklist.
  • The administrator's defaults in Settings → Clone / Migrate (dummy-IP rules and the copy-profile default). Factory defaults: 10 → 240, 162 → 241, fallback 203.0.113.9, copy the profile on.
  • For file-backed objects (XML/JSON schema, DTD, WSDL, OpenAPI, gRPC IDL, Lua script): their content stored in SATOM (see WAF artifacts).

Permissions#

Task Required
Open the dialog, run the checklist, preview, apply config_write — any of network.edit, network.apply, protection.edit, protection.apply or another key that implies it (Operator, Administrator)
Open a clone report config_write, and either the user who started the job or users.manage
Edit Settings → Clone / Migrate users.manage (Administrator)

🔑Permission — Without config_write

The Server Policy list shows no Clone, Clone to, Migrate to, Enable, Disable or Delete button, so the clone and migrate dialogs are not offered. A clone report owned by someone else answers This clone report is not available (unknown job or no access).

ℹ️Note

Changed in 3.1.0: Clone, Clone to and Migrate to run on the Server Policy list itself (FortiWeb → Policy → Server Policy, formerly Loadbalancer → Server Policy): select or tick rows and press the toolbar button. They used to send you to SATOM's classic policy list (?classic=1); that list, with its ⋮ row menu and bulk bar, is gone. The dialog, its preview and its job are unchanged and now open over the list you are on.

How to use#

  1. 1Open the dialogSelect or tick rows, press Clone, Clone to or Migrate to
  2. 2Fill the fieldsDestination, name, VIP, interfaces, profile handling
  3. 3Read the checklistRuns automatically; any red block disables Apply
  4. 4Preview (dry-run)Shows the plan per policy; nothing is written
  5. 5Apply for realStarts a background job
  6. 6Read the reportToast link "View clone report →"

Clone or migrate one policy#

  1. Open FortiWeb → Policy → Server Policy, click the policy's row (or tick its checkbox) and press Clone, Clone to or Migrate to. The dialog (Clone (same box), Clone to another FortiWeb or Migrate to another FortiWeb) opens over the list with that policy filled in.
  2. For a cross-box action, pick the Destination FortiWeb.
  3. Check New policy name.
  4. Check VIP IP for the copy. The hint shows the source VIP and the address suggested by the admin rules, which is prefilled. An empty box at the time of Apply keeps the source address; note that every checklist run refills an empty box with the suggestion.
  5. If Interface binding on the destination appears, choose the destination port for each source port. Each option shows the port's address and the role declared for it; a port that does not exist there is marked missing.
  6. Leave Only add what is missing ticked unless you want rows added to objects the destination already has.
  7. Copy Web Protection Profile shows the administrator's default and is locked. Tick Override admin defaults to change it for this run only.
  8. Read the Pre-flight checklist. Changing the destination, the name, an interface, the profile options, Only add what is missing or the file-backed acknowledgement re-runs it; Re-run checks runs it by hand.
  9. Press Preview (dry-run). Each policy shows ready or its problem, the counts (to create, already exists, total) and the plan.
  10. Press Apply for real. The dialog closes and a job toast tracks progress.

Clone or migrate several policies#

  1. Tick the policies (the header box selects every visible row). The toolbar counts N selected.
  2. Press Clone, Clone to or Migrate to: one dialog and one bulk run for every ticked policy.
  3. No name or VIP is asked: each copy's VIP gets a dummy IP from the admin rules (the dialog shows the rule summary), and a same-box copy is named <name>-copy.
  4. Continue from step 5 above.

When the destination profile differs#

If the destination already has a Web Protection Profile with the same name but different values, the checklist line is a choice and the dialog offers:

  • Use the destination's existing profile (accepting its differing values) — the profile is not copied; the copy binds the destination's profile.
  • Copy the source profile under a new name (selected by default) — the name defaults to <profile>-<source device>.

In a bulk run the field below the choice asks for a SUFFIX instead of a name. When the source profile is copied, the suffix is appended to the name of each differing profile.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: bulk clones now use the profile SUFFIX you type; before, it was dropped and the copies bound the destination's existing profile.

File-backed objects#

FortiWeb keeps only the name of schema, DTD, WSDL, OpenAPI, gRPC IDL and Lua objects in its configuration. The File-backed objects (content, not configuration) table shows each one as will be copied, on destination or no content. When content is missing, Apply for real stays disabled until you either upload the file (see WAF artifacts) or tick Clone anyway — SKIP the objects whose file content is unavailable. Skipped objects are not created; a rule that references one fails (-651), and a migrate does not disable the source.

The table also lists the XML Schemas that a WSDL or XML Schema in the plan imports, with the file that imports each one. FortiWeb refuses a file whose imported schemas aren't on the device yet, so the clone creates them first (or leaves them alone if the destination already has them). An imported schema SATOM can't supply counts as missing content, and the files that import it are skipped.

Fields the destination build adds#

When the destination firmware serves fields the source build never had, the table Fields the destination build adds (optional) lists them with their Evidence (measured or vendor claims). Nothing is set unless you fill a Value; values are validated against the destination build and are applied only to objects this run creates. Changing a value clears the preview.

Configuration#

Settings → Clone / Migrate (administrators)

Field Description Required Example
Dummy-IP transformation rules (first match wins) IP starts with (octets) → Replace with. 1–3 leading octets, same count on both sides, each 0–255. A blank row removes a rule. No 198.51 → 203.0
Fallback dummy IP (no rule matches) Used when no rule matches. Must be a valid IPv4 address. Yes 203.0.113.9
Copy the Web Protection Profile by default on clone / migrate Initial state of Copy Web Protection Profile in the dialog. No on

Press Save clone/migrate rules. The flash reads Clone/Migrate rules saved (N IP rules).

Pre-flight checklist — one block per policy:

Check Levels
Source tree synced live & complete ok / block (unreachable, policy not found, incomplete tree)
Same physical device (different ADOMs of one chassis) warn
Destination reachable ok / warn (falls back to the local copy)
Name of the copy free on the destination ok / warn / block
Web Protection Profile missing / identical / different ok / choice / warn / block (missing and not copied)
VIP address of the copy ok / warn (address already used by a VIP)
TLS certificates warn (key material does not move over REST)
Interface bindings ok / warn / block (port missing on destination)
File-backed objects ok / warn
Capacity on the destination ok / block
API surface: source build → destination build ok / warn / block

Example#

🧪Example — Migrate a policy to a new appliance

pol-shop runs on fweb-01 with VIP 192.0.2.10; it must move to fweb-02.

  1. On fweb-01's Server Policy list, select pol-shop and press Migrate to; pick the destination fweb-02. The name stays pol-shop; no rule matches 192.0.2, so the VIP suggestion is the fallback 203.0.113.9.
  2. The checklist warns Policy uses TLS certificates: upload the certificate on fweb-02 before cutover.
  3. Preview (dry-run) → ready; Apply for real.
  4. The job ends with Migrate to another FortiWeb applied to 1/1 server policy. pol-shop exists disabled on fweb-02 and is disabled on fweb-01.
  5. At cutover, change the copy's VIP to the production address and enable it on fweb-02 (see Server Policy workspace).

Result#

  • A background job titled <Action> — N server policies on <source>. It can be stopped between policies; it never runs two policies at once.
  • One audit entry per policy (policy.clone_here, policy.clone_to, policy.migrate_to) and one summary entry; a notification <Action>: ok/total server policies ok for the user who started it.
  • A Clone history badge on the source row with every copy (Cloned here as, Cloned to, Migrated to), when, by whom, and the reason of any failure.
  • The Clone / Migrate result report at /workspace/clone-report/<job_id>, linked from the job toast (View clone report →) and the Job Manager. Per policy it shows planned to create, created, already existed, failed, not found on device after write, could not verify and rows not added, and a full table with plan, result and On device (✓ present, ✗ missing, ? unverifiable).
  • A partial clone is left disabled on the destination; nothing is rolled back. Re-running skips what already exists.

Troubleshooting#

"Name "" already exists on "#

Possible causes — the copy's name is taken on the destination.

Solution — change New policy name (single) or clone one at a time.

Verification — the line reads Name "<name>" is free on <device>.

"Source is not reachable" or "Source tree is INCOMPLETE — N missing object(s)"#

Possible causes - The source device does not answer, or objects referenced by the policy did not resolve live.

Solution 1. Check the source appliance; repair or re-create the missing objects listed. 2. Press Re-run checks.

Verification — Source tree synced live & complete.

"WPP "" is NOT on "#

Possible causes — Copy Web Protection Profile is off and the destination lacks the profile.

Solution — tick Override admin defaults and Copy Web Protection Profile, or create the profile on the destination first.

"Interface does not exist on "#

Solution — choose an existing destination port in Interface binding on the destination, or create the port first. A warning Interface exists on <device> — purpose NOT declared means the port names match but no role is declared; set the role on both devices (Appliances → Edit → Interfaces).

"VIP IP '' is not a valid IPv4 address"#

Solution — enter a plain IPv4 address.

"N object(s) failed: …" or "… — source left live"#

Possible causes — the destination refused one or more objects. For a migrate, the source stays enabled.

Solution 1. Open the clone report and read Failed objects. 2. Fix the cause and run the clone again; existing objects are skipped.

Verification — the report shows success.

"nothing to create — "" exists"#

Possible causes — a same-box clone found every object already present.

Solution — choose a different New policy name.

Migrate finished but the source is still enabled#

Possible causes - File-backed objects were skipped, or Only add what is missing held rows back (rows not added). The copy is then not equivalent, so the source is left enabled on purpose.

Solution — complete the destination (upload the files, or add the rows), then disable the source by hand.

Clone to and Migrate to are disabled#

Possible causes — no other FortiWeb is visible to you (hovering the buttons shows No other FortiWeb is registered), or no row is selected.

Solution — register the destination FortiWeb (see Appliances), or check that it is not in maintenance mode. Select or tick at least one policy.

Advanced#

Advanced Opening the dialog from a link

/workspace/<appliance_id>?act=<action>&policy=<name> opens the Server Policy list with the dialog already open for that policy. The old address /web/workspace/<appliance_id> opens the same list and keeps the act and policy parameters.

Advanced Same-box clones share objects

A same-box clone creates a new server policy root. Objects that already exist on the box — virtual server, VIP, pool, profile — are classified as existing and reused, not duplicated. The VIP rewrite only applies to VIP objects a run creates; an existing VIP is never changed.

Advanced Rows in objects the destination already has

With Only add what is missing off, rows missing under an existing object are added, and a row whose unique key exists with different content is updated in place (the destination row with the source's non-empty fields laid over it). With it on, those rows are held back and listed as untouched in the plan and as Rows NOT added (additive mode) in the report.

Advanced Options accepted by the endpoint but not shown in the dialog

The apply and preview requests also accept: reconcile_rows (default on; off refuses a run with keyed collisions), dst_wpp (bind an existing destination profile under another name), wpp_only_if_missing, wpp_decisions (the answer to the read-only comparison at POST /workspace/<id>/policy-action/wpp-compare), copy_cert_material (carry certificate key material over the CLI), probe_backends / probe_ssh (reachability of the real servers after the write) and analyse_workers (1–10 parallel readers for a preview only). The profile options are mutually exclusive, and combining "only add what is missing" with wpp_decisions is refused.

Advanced Profiles in bulk runs

Within one bulk run, a profile already carried for an earlier policy (same source profile, same landing name) is not walked again: later policies only create it if it is still missing.
